newsitem.title: SPAIN: Spain's Aznar says EMU, jobs top goal in second year.
newsitem.headline: Spain's Aznar says EMU, jobs top goal in second year.

text.p: Spanish Prime Minister Jose Maria Aznar said on Monday in an interview that Spain's integration into Europe, along with employment, welfare and state reform were the areas of concentration for his second year in power.

Aznar, in the second of a two-part interview with newspaper El Mundo, reiterated his belief that Spain would be among the first countries to join Europe's monetary union, adding he hoped the calendar for putting the euro into play was not delayed.
"I will do everything possible so that this does not occur. All of the countries have to overcome one difficulty or another. But I hope the calendar is strictly followed," he said.
The Spanish leader said inflation in Spain would be reduced gradually during the next 12 months until it reached a level below two percent in 1998.
"At the end of this year, it (inflation) will be at 2.2 or 2.3 percent. But very probably within a year we will see inflation below two percent," Aznar said.
He said he hoped to provide an economic climate that was healthy enough to create one million jobs by the year 2000, adding some 200,000 to 250,000 each year.
